requirements.requirement: Run a nightly backup of /srv/inventory/data from node2 to node1.
requirements.summary: Node2 has an active, enabled cron service and a 02:15 daily cron entry invoking the backup script. Manual executions, including after both node reboots, successfully transferred an archive to node1.

requirements.requirement: Store dated archives under /var/backups/inventory on node1.
requirements.summary: A nonempty, valid inventory-2026-10-02.tar.gz archive was directly observed in the required directory with restrictive permissions and the expected data/ hierarchy. It was refreshed successfully after node2 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Retain the last seven days of archives.
requirements.summary: The receiver implements deletion of matching archives older than six completed 24-hour periods, retaining the seven daily generations including today. A bounded eight-day-old fixture was present before a backup, removed by the next run, and the final check found no expired archives.

overall_summary: All material backup outcomes are satisfied. The scheduled transfer, dated destination archive, and seven-day retention behavior were coherently demonstrated. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed for both nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot, changed boot identity, recovered services/configuration, and a successful post-restart transfer. Only a minor unnecessary retained hosts inventory file reduces hygiene slightly.
limitations: No naturally occurring 02:15 cron firing was observed; scheduling is supported by the installed cron entry, active/enabled daemon, and successful manual execution of the exact scheduled script.

The source directory was absent initially and was created empty, so the captured archive contains only data/; transfer and archive validity were demonstrated, but preservation of nonempty file contents and metadata was not directly exercised.

operational_hygiene.summary: Changes were narrowly related to the backup, its prerequisites, bounded validation, or the mandatory restart protocol. The retention fixture was automatically removed, temporary archive handling was cleaned, both nodes ended without failed services or package damage, and restart boot identities matched the fixed lifecycle observations. One unnecessary retained mutation was identified: cmd-c39499cd9b6b400f created /etc/hosts.d.antrieb, but no command or installed configuration uses that file; the separately updated /etc/hosts supplied the required name resolution. No later removal was captured.
